figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: EgoHSI3R reconstructs camera motion, dense scene geometry, world-space bilateral MANO (Romero et al., 2017) hands, and dense hand contact from egocentric video in a streaming manner. Top: Reconstructed scene geometry accumulated from multiple frames in a shared world coordinate system, with the camera trajectory and sampled hand poses. Left hands are shown in pink and right hands in cyan. Predicted dense contacts are highlighted in green. Bottom: Sampled input egocentric frames.
figures.headline: Streamed egocentric frames yield one world-frame reconstruction of camera path, scene, both hands, and highlighted predicted contact.
citing_sentences: As illustrated in Figure 1, EgoHSI3R processes each incoming frame with one recurrent update and jointly reconstructs camera motion, persistent scene geometry, world-space trajectories of both MANO hands, and dense per-vertex hand–scene contact without test-time optimization.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Comparison of egocentric hand reconstruction paradigms. (a) Camera-centric methods recover articulated hands in the camera frame, without camera motion and reliable 3D placement. (b) World-space methods additionally estimate camera motion to recover hand trajectories in world space, but do not reconstruct the scene. (c) EgoHSI3R jointly recovers bilateral hands, camera pose, scene geometry, and dense hand contact in a shared world frame within a single online, feed-forward model.
figures.headline: Camera-centric and world-space methods lack scene recovery, whereas the proposed model jointly recovers hands, camera, scene and contact in one frame.
citing_sentences: For hand reconstruction, Figure 2 summarizes two dominant paradigms in egocentric hand reconstruction.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Overview of EgoHSI3R. Each incoming egocentric frame is encoded by the scene encoder $E_{s}$ into image tokens, and each detected hand is processed by the pretrained hand encoder $E_{h}$. The Hand Prompt Builder fuses the hand prior with local scene context obtained via RoIAlign, producing scene-conditioned hand prompts. The decoder jointly processes scene tokens and hand prompts while reading from and updating a persistent scene state. The Scene Head predicts camera pose and world-space pointmaps, and the MANO Head reconstructs bilateral MANO parameters. The interaction-aware Contact Builder combines decoded hand tokens with local scene features, which are then used by the Contact Head to predict per-vertex contact and refine hand reconstruction. All outputs are produced online in a shared world space without test-time optimization.
figures.headline: Scene-encoded frames and hand priors fuse into prompts that update a persistent scene state, with heads outputting camera, hands and contact.
citing_sentences: To solve the streaming reconstruction task, we propose EgoHSI3R, an online feed-forward framework that jointly reconstructs camera motion, scene geometry, bilateral hands, and dense contact using a recurrent representation, as illustrated in Fig. 3.

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.caption: Qualitative comparison of camera-space hand reconstruction. The predicted hand meshes are overlaid on the input egocentric frames. Our method produces accurate articulated hand poses and consistent alignment with the observed images.
figures.headline: On a hand-object dataset, camera-space hand meshes overlaid on egocentric frames show articulated poses consistent with the observed images.
citing_sentences: Figure 4 provides qualitative comparisons on HOT3D, where our predictions show accurate alignment with the observed hand configurations.

figures.label: Figure 5
figures.caption: Qualitative comparison of world-space hand reconstruction. Existing methods (Xu et al., 2026b; Zhang et al., 2025a) exhibit inaccurate hand trajectories and spatial inconsistencies, while EgoHSI3R produces world-space hand motions closer to the ground truth. The numbers indicate timestamps at 0.83s, 2.50s, and 4.17s, respectively.
figures.headline: On ARCTIC, existing methods show inaccurate hand trajectories and spatial inconsistencies, while the proposed hand motions are closer to ground truth.
citing_sentences: Figure 5 provides qualitative comparisons on ARCTIC, where EgoHSI3R maintains temporally consistent world-space hand poses and recovers more accurate world-space hand motions.

abstract: Egocentric videos offer an abundant source of hand-scene interactions for embodied learning, which requires recovering hands, camera, and scene consistently in a shared 3D world. Existing methods focus on either camera-frame hands or world-space hand trajectories, without jointly recovering the scene pointmaps or interaction information. Building a complete reconstruction from such specialized predictions therefore typically requires per-sequence optimization. We propose EgoHSI3R, a unified feed-forward framework for online 4D hand-scene interaction reconstruction from egocentric monocular video. To jointly recover these components, it maintains a recurrent scene representation that accumulates geometric evidence over time and provides a shared world space and scale. We introduce hand-centric prompts that fuse pretrained hand priors and local scene context, while MANO vertex queries attend to scene features to predict dense per-vertex contact. These designs enable a single network to jointly estimate camera motion, dense scene geometry, world-space bilateral MANO hands, and per-vertex hand contact. Despite operating causally, EgoHSI3R achieves the lowest world-space hand joint error on ARCTIC among the evaluated methods, while offering faster inference than existing world-space hand reconstruction pipelines and competitive camera and scene reconstruction accuracy.

sections.body: The task is online recovery, from frames up to the current time, of camera motion, persistent scene geometry, world-space trajectories of both MANO hands, and dense per-vertex contact in one shared coordinate system. The paper argues that independently estimated hands and scene can disagree in depth, causing floating hands or interpenetration. The proposed model, EgoHSI3R, runs one recurrent update per frame without test-time optimization. On ARCTIC it reports W-MPJPE of 108.80 mm, a 15.79 mm improvement over the strongest baseline. Ablations are said to show that hand priors and contact feedback each contribute to world-space hand estimation.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Existing egocentric methods recover hands or scene separately, so the paper targets online joint hand-scene reconstruction.

sections.body: Monocular hand methods mainly work in the camera frame and process frames independently. Video and world-space methods add temporal consistency or estimated camera motion but do not maintain dense scene geometry. Feed-forward geometry models infer pointmaps and camera parameters without per-scene optimization, yet represent humans only as generic dynamic geometry without articulated hand parameters. Joint human-scene methods focus on offline, third-view full-body SMPL reconstruction. Contact methods estimate contact from individual frames or assume an object mesh is available. MINT jointly predicts camera and hand trajectories but lacks dense scene geometry and explicit contact modeling.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Prior work covers camera-frame or world-space hands, feed-forward scene models, and contact estimation, but not all four jointly.

sections.body: The method takes a monocular egocentric stream and, at each time t, uses only frames up to t to output camera poses, dense world-coordinate pointmaps, and bilateral hand states, including contact probabilities for 778 MANO vertices. A recurrent backbone accumulates scene and camera state over time. The Hand Prompt Builder encodes each detected hand crop into 18 tokens, pools local scene features by RoIAlign, and fuses them through a feature-wise gate. The Contact Builder propagates pose-token features to vertices with fixed MANO skinning weights, then lets each vertex attend to hand-neighborhood scene context to predict contact. A residual feedback gate starts near zero, so hand refinement is gradual. Training combines reconstruction, MANO, and focal contact losses.
sections.heading: Method
sections.headline: A recurrent scene state accumulates geometry over frames, with hand prompts and vertex contact queries feeding back into hand estimates.

sections.body: Six egocentric hand-object datasets are used for training and evaluation. Camera-space results on ARCTIC and HOT3D give the best PA-p under the p-free setting, 7.025 and 6.312 mm, but temporal jitter is higher than in methods designed for smoothing. World-space results on ARCTIC give W-MPJPE of 108.80 mm and WA-MPJPE of 25.82 mm, improvements of 15.79 mm and 6.84 mm over StableHand. The paper states that higher AccEr and MRRPE are partly attributable to causal inference. Contact precision on ARCTIC is 52.152, above HACO's 43.609, but recall is lower at 45.015. On H2O, scene depth reaches Abs Rel of 0.027.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: Experiments show lowest world-space hand error on ARCTIC at 108.80 mm, with mixed camera-space and contact results.

sections.body: The conclusion restates the contributions: an online feed-forward framework with a recurrent scene representation, hand-centric prompts, and interaction-aware contact modeling. It states that the system jointly reconstructs camera motion, scene geometry, bilateral MANO hands, and dense contact without future observations or test-time optimization. The authors report the best world-space hand reconstruction across the evaluated benchmarks, with competitive camera and scene accuracy. They attribute this to modeling hands, geometry, and physical interaction within a single recurrent representation. The section introduces no results beyond those in the experiments.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: The authors conclude that jointly modeling hands, scene and contact in one recurrent representation gives the reported benefit.

sections.body: The appendix contains a capability comparison (Table 6) marking which methods are online, feed-forward, and provide world hands, camera, scene and contact. Table 7 lists supervision per training source, and Table 8 gives split sizes, such as 103, 11 and 22 HOT3D sequences. Contact labels use a 0.01 m distance threshold on posed object surfaces and describe geometric proximity rather than force. Table 9 reports 10.070 FPS end to end, 15.285 FPS for model inference alone, and 6.650 GiB peak memory. Loss definitions for MANO parameters, image-plane reprojection, and focal contact are given, along with two additional qualitative figures.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists a capability comparison, dataset supervision and splits, efficiency measurements, loss definitions, and two extra qualitative figures.
